title: IS6110, IS1081, and Ultra’s extra ears
dek: Xpert Ultra added multi-copy IS6110/IS1081 to the rpoB beacons. Trace calls are often IS-driven. Fingerprinting with IS6110 RFLP is historical; copy number still matters for LOD.
story: IS6110 is an MTBC-typical insertion sequence, usually 1–25 copies, absent or rare in most NTM. IS1081 is more copy-stable. Xpert MTB/RIF interrogated rpoB. Ultra added IS6110 and IS1081 amplification so paucibacillary DNA still rings the bell — that is why trace exists as a semi-quantitative band below “very low.”

Trace plus RIF-indeterminate means the IS targets fired and the RRDR beacons did not have enough template. Prior-treated lungs can shed DNA for months. Children and extrapulmonary sites live in this band on purpose.

IS6110 RFLP was the 1990s outbreak tool. WGS SNP distances replaced it. Copy-number variation still confounds mapping near insertion sites and still explains why some L1 strains with few IS6110 copies have a slightly different Ultra LOD than L2.
deepTitle: Do not speciate from a single IS hit
deep: Some NTM harbour IS6110-like elements. Speciation is a tree plus RD markers, not one BLAST hit.
M. bovis BCG has IS6110; Ultra can detect BCG DNA in urine after bladder instillation. RD1 is the BCG discriminator, not IS6110.
De-duplication of multi-mapping IS reads will punch holes in a BAM. Do not call those holes “deletions” without mates and coverage context.
Spoligotyping (CRISPR/DR) is another historical barcode. Lineage SNP barcodes superseded it for routine genomics.

visual.caption: Cartoon LOD: rpoB-only cartridges need more genomes than IS-augmented Ultra. Trace is the IS-only neighbourhood, not a smear grade.

example.title: Trace in a BCG bladder patient
example.setup: Urology patient, Ultra on urine “MTB trace, RIF indeterminate.” No pulmonary symptoms.

steps.title: IS targets do not equal pulmonary TB
steps.body: BCG is MTBC. Trace IS signal in urine after instillation is expected chemistry.

steps.title: Speciate
steps.body: RD1 deletion / BCG SNPs. Do not start HRZE from a trace urine.

steps.title: RIF indeterminate is not RR
steps.body: Insufficient RRDR template, not a disputed rpoB mutation.

example.takeaway: Ultra hears IS elements. Trace is a limit-of-detection object, not a smear.

choices: Replace rpoB as the RIF target
Lower the limit of detection for MTBC DNA
check.answer: Lower the limit of detection for MTBC DNA
check.why: Multi-copy IS elements fire when rpoB template is scarce. RIF still needs RRDR.

whyWrong.Detect NTM specifically: IS6110 is an MTBC-ish marker, imperfectly.

check.prompt: If a strain has ~1 IS6110 copy versus ~20, Ultra’s IS-driven LOD is expected to be:
choices: Worse (higher LOD) for the low-copy strain
check.answer: Worse (higher LOD) for the low-copy strain
check.why: Fewer IS templates per genome means the IS-only trace band is harder to reach. Lineage 1 is the usual teaching example.

whyWrong.Identical by definition: Copy number is the point of IS targets.
whyWrong.Independent of copy number always: rpoB is copy-1; IS is not.

check.why: That is the cartridge change that created trace.
